CENTRAL Station.
December 20th, 1915.
16/4/18
REPORT ON a Norweigan subject named Renby.
Made by D.S.I.Burnside. Forwarded by
Sir,
I beg to report having been informed that a Norweigan
subject named Renby, employed by Messrs Melchers & Coy as Captain
of the s.s."Hsin Fung" is now residing in the Astor House Hotel
& a short time ago was paid a sum of $10.000 by Germans in order
that he should keep quiet over some shipment of cargo which he,
together with a German, successfully dealt with (shipped) in
Shanghai & it is now understood that Renby is demanding more
money in the shape of blackmail & that the cargo consisted of
arms etc:
Your obedient servant,
J. Burnside.
Det: Sub Insp.
KPD
21/12
Chief Detective Inspector.
Everett returned to Shanghai from Shanghai Series 7/4/19.

18/4/16
关于一名名为 Renby 的挪威籍人士的报告。
由副巡官 Burnside 撰写。呈送
先生，
谨此报告，据 inform 称，受雇于美最时洋行（Messrs Melchers & Coy）担任“新丰”轮（s.s. "Hsin Fung"）船长的挪威籍人士 Renby，现居住于礼查饭店（Astor House Hotel），且不久前曾从德国人处收取一笔10,000美元的款项，以要求他对某批货物保持沉默；该批货物是他与一名德国人在上海成功处理（装运）的。目前据悉，Renby 正以勒索的形式索要更多钱财，且该批货物由武器等组成：
您顺从的仆人，
J. Burnside.
侦探副巡官。
KPD
12/21
首席侦探巡官。
Everett 于 1919年4月7日 从上海系列返回上海。

REPORT ON S/S Shantung Mary
Made by Inspt. Eck. Forwarded by
Sir,
The S/S Shantung Mary was bought by
Chow, on Haven to 5 Hongkong Road acting as agent.
The ship has been here for some time there being some
dispute between the buyers and sellers, and according
to reports the deal may fall through. The Customs searched
the ship but found nothing. It is believed that she is to be
used for the exportation of arms, if the purchase is arranged.
The Customs will keep her under close observation.
Your obedient servant
A. Eck.
C.D.I.

S. M. POLICE
REGISTER
No. 3101
Date 3. 11. 15.

November 3rd

The Captain Superintendent of Police.

Sir,
The "Shinten Maru", which is at present in the International Dock, is said to be ostensibly owned by Chinese, but is chartered by A. Nielsen.
The Captain's name is Randbey. He is a Dane who has been living in the Astor House for some time, his expenses being paid by Nielsen.
The Chief Officer is a Norwegian named Thorgensen who lives at the boarding house of Mrs Diedrichsen, No. 12 North Szechuen Road, and he gives information to the effect that if the Customs House people examine the cargo throughly, they will get a surprise.
He has been engaged in Shanghai, has drawn his pay for two months, but has only been to the ship on one occasion when he went on board to have a look round.
She should have sailed about three weeks ago but has been held back, he thinks, on account of the recent seizure of arms by the Municipal Police.
He does not know the ship's destination.

Your obedient servant,

Chief Detective Inspector,

先生，
目前停泊在国际码头的“新天丸”轮（Shinten Maru），据称名义上为中国人所有，但实际上由 A. Nielsen 承租。
船长名为 Randbey。他是一名丹麦人，已在礼查饭店居住了一段时间，费用由 Nielsen 支付。
首席大副是一名名为 Thorgensen 的挪威人，居住在北四川路12号 Diedrichsen 太太的寄宿公寓，他提供信息称，如果海关人员彻底检查货物，他们会大吃一惊。
他在上海受雇，已领取两个月的薪水，但只去过船上一次，即登船巡视。
该船本应于约三周前启航，但他认为由于近期工部局警务处查获武器而被扣留。
他不知道船的目的地。

您顺从的仆人，

首席侦探巡官，

November 1st 5

Sir,
Japanese interpreter Nakai reports that he has
information to the effect that 14 barrels stored in the
N.Y.K. No.2 godown and declared to be filled with cement
contain, 400 Browning and 600 mauser pistols with 100
rounds of ammunition for each.
There are more than 200 barrels of cement in No.2
godown belonging to various owners and it is impossible
to say which of the 14 contain the pistols.

Your Obedient Servant,

Chief Detective Inspector.

Captain Superintendent of Police.

Central Police Station.
30th October 1915

REPORT ON further enquiries re Nielsen.

Made by D.S.I. Brewster Forwarded by

Sir

I have now ascertained that Nielsen, the German implicated
in the Harbin Road arms case, runs a small motor boat named the
Nina, in which he makes frequent visits to Pootung and also up and
down the River. One of these trips was made last Saturday eve-
ning when it was raining heavily and a pleasure trip out of the
question. It is possible that he uses the boat to communicate
with a depot for the storage of arms, the existence of which,
somewhere outside the settlement, seems certain.

Your Obedient Servant
（签名）
D.S.I.

Chief Det Insp.

Returned with many thanks.
2/11

关于对 Nielsen 进一步调查的报告。

由副巡官 Brewster 撰写 呈送由

先生

我现在查明，卷入哈宾路武器案的德国人 Nielsen 经营着一艘名为“尼娜”号（Nina）的小型摩托艇，他经常乘坐该艇往返浦东及沿河上下。上周六晚上他就进行了一次这样的行程，当时雨下得很大，不可能是为了游玩。他有可能利用该艇与租界外某处的武器储存库联络，该储存库的存在似乎是确定的。

您顺从的仆人
（签名）
D.S.I.

首席侦探巡官。

已归还，多谢。

October 20th 1916
（印：SHANGHAI MUNICIPAL COUNCIL POLICE FORCE. (DETECTIVE BRANCH.)）
Sir,
It is reported that the s.s. Rio Pasig referred to
on attached newspaper cutting is taking on board copper
and leather the destination of which is Germany.
It is rather significant that the office of Everett
the agent for the steamer is next to that occupied by Nielsen
at 1A Jinkee Road and that Tong Ts Dong 董贄塘 the man
arrested at Harbin Road Station who was doing Nielsen's
work in connection with the intended shipment of arms had
in his possession a number of papers showing that he was
making certain arrangements with Everett in connection
with shipping.
Your Obedient Servant,
William Armstrong
Chief Detective Inspector.
Captain Superintendent of Police.
